why: Radiography detects planar cracks well when the crack plane is parallel to the beam (the beam traverses the crack depth); it misses cracks whose plane is perpendicular to the beam. The table states the opposite limitation.
evidence: NDT Resource Center (nde-ed.org), Radiographic Testing: planar flaws must be aligned roughly parallel to the radiation beam to be detected; cracks perpendicular to the beam give little density change. Same in ASNT/ISO 17636 practice (beam angle chosen along expected crack planes).

new: 4. چرا پرتونگاری ترکی را که صفحه‌اش عمود بر پرتو است خوب نمی‌بیند، اما ترکِ موازی با پرتو را می‌بیند؟
why: Self-check question built on the same reversed fact as the NDT table: radiography sees cracks parallel to the beam and misses those perpendicular to it.
evidence: See previous finding; the change in transmitted thickness through a thin crack is largest when the beam runs along the crack plane.
